solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Island broadcasting live takes

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: to live is to be, to exist
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A radio station on some island takes its programmes live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live takes' reads like broadcasting jargon, but 'live' is BE and 'takes' puts ON AIR inside it. Bonaire is the B of the Dutch Caribbean ABC islands, one of this puzzle's five ABC trios.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaire is a Dutch Caribbean island lying off the Venezuelan coast, beside Aruba and Curaçao.

clue.text: Having put away billion, pipe in Head’s riches

indicators.note: something put away is removed from view, so a letter is taken out
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for billion
bonce is British slang for the head, plus the S of the possessive
to pule is to cry thinly, to pipe or whimper

explanation.surface: Someone has banked a billion and now smokes a pipe amid the headmaster's wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for head; drop its B to leave ONCE'S, then put PULE inside. 'Pipe' looks like the smoker's object but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth or luxury, and the plural form stands for riches in general.

clue.text: Resistance encountered by a man in a state

indicators.note: what is encountered by something meets it coming the other way, so it is placed straight after it

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a gent is a gentleman, a man
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man in some troubled state meets resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance encountered by a' means R comes after the first A. Argentina is the A of the South American ABC countries, another of the puzzle's trios.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a sovereign country, and state is the general word for an independent nation.

clue.text: Pleasurable brews: pub’s withdrawing Mr Protz’s favourite

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the answer

indicators.note: what is withdrawing is pulling out, so those letters leave
brewing stirs ingredients into something new, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters of the word, possessive S included

explanation.surface: A beer writer praises enjoyable brews while a pub withdraws his favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, U, B, S from PLEASURABLE to leave LEARALE, then rearrange. Roger Protz is a British beer writer long associated with the Campaign for Real Ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Protz championed traditional cask-conditioned beer, the drink he is best known for promoting in Britain.

clue.text: Liqueur business collects strain extracted from araucaria growing wild

indicators.note: what is extracted is pulled out, so those letters are removed
a plant growing wild sprawls in no set order, so the letters are rearranged
to collect is to gather up and hold, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
taken as written; the araucaria is the monkey-puzzle tree
a strain is a melody, and an aria is a song

explanation.surface: A drinks firm gathers an extract from a wild monkey-puzzle tree to flavour its liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests a plant variety but means a tune, and the araucaria is the monkey-puzzle tree. Curaçao is the C of the ABC islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Curaçao is an orange-flavoured liqueur named after the Caribbean island where its bitter oranges grow.

clue.text: Ovine females and a bovine male reportedly functional

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.clueFragment: Ovine females and a bovine male
blocks.note: ovine females are ewes, and a bovine male is a bull

explanation.surface: Some sheep and a bull are said to be in working order on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'ewes a bull' quickly and you hear a word meaning fit for use.
explanation.definitionFit: Something functional works and can be put to practical service, which is exactly the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Academy run, off and on, out by a Caribbean location

indicators.note: something off and on comes and goes, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for academy
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run
the second, fourth and sixth letters of these words

explanation.surface: A college track has been closed off and on, out near a Caribbean spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make 'off and on' look like a description of the run; it tells you to take alternate letters of 'out by a'. Aruba is the A of the ABC islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Aruba is a Dutch Caribbean island off Venezuela, so it is literally a place in the Caribbean.

clue.text: An urge to leave the same excuse

indicators.note: what leaves goes away, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: an urge, specifically a sexual one, is a libido
DO is short for ditto, the same

explanation.surface: An urge to walk out is offered as the same old excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the short form of ditto, used in lists to mean 'the same'. Remove it from A LIBIDO. Alibi starts the crime trio alibi, burglar, corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used more loosely for any justification offered to avoid blame.

clue.text: Authentic food for backsliding Scrubs drug thief

indicators.note: to backslide is to slip backwards, so the letters run the other way
to scrub something is to cancel or wipe it out, so a letter goes

blocks.note: authentic means real
grub is slang for food
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A thief who has relapsed on drugs is served real food in Wormwood Scrubs prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a London prison, which makes 'Scrubs' look like a proper noun; here it means deletes. Reverse REAL GRUB, then remove E.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar is a criminal who breaks into buildings to steal, a particular kind of robber.

clue.text: Virtuoso players united in taking overture to Halle

indicators.note: an overture opens a piece, so only the opening letter is kept
the word before takes on the next piece, which joins directly onto its front

blocks.note: players in a team are men
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
the first letter of the orchestra's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Star musicians join together to play the overture with the Hallé, Manchester's orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hallé is an orchestra, so the musical surface feels whole; the definition is just the first word. Yehudi Menuhin was a famous violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: Yehudi Menuhin was a celebrated violinist, and a virtuoso is a performer of exceptional technical skill.

clue.text: In actual fact it grows in Spain and North Africa

definitions.text: it grows in Spain and North Africa

indicators.note: what is in a phrase sits inside it, spread across the words

blocks.note: the letters running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A factual statement about a plant's native range in the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In actual fact' reads like a filler phrase; it holds the answer. Alfa is also the A of the NATO alphabet alfa, bravo, charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfa is esparto grass, a tough wild grass native to Spain and North Africa used for paper and rope.

clue.text: Writer Jack molested up a lane

indicators.note: something molested is roughly interfered with, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Jack is attacked up a lane, and a writer reports it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Paul was the pen name of the German novelist Johann Paul Friedrich Richter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Paul was a German Romantic novelist and humorist, so he is an example of a writer.

clue.text: NUT discussed supporter’s misfortune

indicators.note: what is discussed is talked about out loud, so the sound counts

blocks.note: a bra is a supporter, and ill is misfortune, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: The National Union of Teachers talks over a supporter's bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make NUT look like the teachers' union; it is a plain nut. A Brazil nut sounds like 'bra's ill'. Brazil is also the B of the ABC countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil is the large three-sided nut of a South American tree, so it is an example of a nut.

clue.text: Baroness Smith of Basildon’s abbreviated records

blocks.note: first meaning: her government post, Lord Privy Seal, in short form
second meaning: long-playing vinyl discs

explanation.walkthrough: Baroness Smith of Basildon became Lord Privy Seal and Leader of the House of Lords in 2024, an old cabinet title usually shortened to three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials of the cabinet office Lord Privy Seal coincide with the plural of long-playing vinyl album discs.

clue.text: Switzerland acquires island from the French nation

indicators.note: what is acquired is added on, so the next piece follows straight after

blocks.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland, from Confoederatio Helvetica
I is the abbreviation for island
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Switzerland takes over an island from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the French' sounds like the island's previous owner; 'the French' is LE and 'from' links. Chile is the C of the ABC countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is an independent South American country, so it is an example of a nation.

clue.text: So five groups here walk in the park?

definitions.note: a noun phrase for something easy; the answer is an adjectival phrase

blocks.note: 'so' as an intensifier, as in 'so simple', stands in for the comparison phrase
this grid holds five trios whose members begin with the first three letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Five groups of people take an easy stroll in the park.
explanation.walkthrough: The five ABC trios are the islands Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao; the countries Argentina, Brazil, Chile; NATO's alfa, bravo, charlie; alibi, burglar, corpse; and Andover, Bexhill, Churston from Agatha Christie's The ABC Murders.
explanation.definitionFit: A walk in the park is something effortless, and the idiom for a very simple task says exactly that.

clue.text: Collides heavily with Hamilton’s rear wing and is almost out

indicators.note: the rear wing is the back edge, so only the final letter is kept
letters put out of place are disordered and must be rearranged

blocks.note: the final letter of the driver's name
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Formula One crash damages Lewis Hamilton's rear wing and nearly puts him out of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear wing' is a real part of an F1 car, which hides the instruction to take Hamilton's last letter. 'Almost' looks like it trims a word but is fodder itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam into something is to crash against it with great force, a phrasal verb for a violent collision.

clue.text: A fine being in balance, put forward defence

definitions.note: the older sense: to argue in one's own defence

indicators.note: something being in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: taken as written
at sea, an offender is logged, that is fined, with the penalty entered in the log
poise is balance or equilibrium

explanation.surface: A defendant weighs up a fine and puts forward a defence.
explanation.walkthrough: In the navy, to log a sailor meant fining him and recording the penalty in the ship's log, which is the fair link to 'fine'.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal defence of one's conduct, and the verb originally meant to speak in vindication rather than to say sorry.

clue.text: Like the impudence of Drake in Iceman?

blocks.note: as means like, in comparisons
sass is cheeky impudence; the rapper Drake is often described as sassy
taken as written

explanation.surface: The cheek of the rapper Drake on his album Iceman.
explanation.walkthrough: Iceman is the title of a Drake album, so the surface hangs together; the question mark flags that it also means someone who ices, slang for kills.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone is slang for murder, so a whimsical iceman is a professional killer who murders for hire.

clue.text: See 16
Intimate, uplifting non-churchy recordings

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up turns the letters so they read from the bottom

blocks.note: laic means of the laity, not clergy
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: Personal, inspiring recordings of secular songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' reads as praise for the music; in a down entry it turns the letters upwards. LAIC is a formal word for lay, not of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A special friend or relationship is a close and personal one, so the two adjectives overlap in that sense.

clue.text: The station bogy

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for a police station
second meaning: a bogy is an evil spirit, and the devil has a traditional nickname that fits

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the nick' is slang for a police station or prison, and Old Nick is a traditional name for the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang for a police lock-up and the folk name of Satan, a bogy or bugbear, share one word.

clue.text: Well done veal ribs, periodically turned over

indicators.note: what happens periodically happens at intervals, so letters are kept at regular gaps
something turned faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Veal ribs cooked well done, turned over from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' looks like the cooking instruction for the meat; it is the cheer. 'Turned over' feels like one phrase but splits into the reversal and O. Bravo is the B of the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is an exclamation of applause, the cry an audience uses to congratulate a fine performance.

clue.text: Liquid fuel apparently refused large swimmer

indicators.note: a liquid flows and takes any shape, so the letters run into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
something refused is binned, and 'binned' is read as in a bin

explanation.surface: Liquid fuel was turned down by some big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' flags a playful reading: rejected stuff is binned, so the shuffled fuel goes inside BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluefin is a big tuna that can exceed two metres, so a large swimmer describes the fish.

clue.text: Sent back key dresses for mummy?

definitions.note: a mummy is one example, hence the question mark

indicators.note: dressing someone wraps clothes round them, so one piece wraps around another
what is sent back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone returns the important dresses bought for their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy' wants to be a mother; it is the embalmed body. 'Key' is a keyboard key here, not a musical one. Corpse completes the trio alibi, burglar, corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian mummy is an embalmed dead body, so it is a particular kind of preserved cadaver.

clue.text: Oxygen taken up in e.g. washing or cleaning pigment

indicators.note: what is taken up is lifted out of its place, and in a down entry up means towards the top

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
washing and cleaning are examples of household chores

explanation.surface: Oxygen is absorbed during laundry or cleaning, which affects a dye.
explanation.walkthrough: The O already sits in CHORE; lift it out and move it to the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown clay used since prehistory as a colouring material for paint.

clue.text: Evil goblin blocking pub doorway

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, filling the gap

blocks.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
an orc is an evil goblin-like creature of fantasy

explanation.surface: A nasty goblin stands in the pub doorway, barring the way in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost literal; the trick is reading 'pub' as the two-letter map abbreviation and 'blocking' as standing inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A porch is a covered shelter built over the entrance to a building, an extended entranceway.

clue.text: Agitator catching last of trains to area of Devon

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so other pieces go inside
the last of something is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a churn agitates milk to make butter
the final letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A troublemaker catches the last train to a part of Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitator' wants to be a rabble-rouser; it is a butter churn. Churston, near Brixham in Devon, is the C town in Agatha Christie's The ABC Murders, after Andover and Bexhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Churston Ferrers is a village and district on Tor Bay in south Devon, so it names a place in that county.

clue.text: One does stretch numpty

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner, someone who does the housework
to stretch the truth is to lie

explanation.surface: Someone who does a prison stretch is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does stretch' suggests serving time; a British char is a cleaning lady who 'does' for a household. Numpty is Scottish slang for an idiot, and a right charlie is a fool. Charlie is also the C of the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a foolish or incompetent person, so they are slang synonyms.

clue.text: Composition using only two notes receiving fine mark over 100

definitions.note: read as a mark divided by a hundred

indicators.note: limiting a word to two of a repeated letter means one copy must go
to receive is to take in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: penning is writing, composing
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A piece of music written with just two notes earns a top mark of over 100.
explanation.walkthrough: N is short for note (as in banknote); PENNING has three, so drop one to leave PENNIG. 'Mark over 100' is a fraction: one hundredth of a German mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The pfennig was the smallest German coin, worth one hundredth of a Deutschmark before the euro arrived.

clue.text: Spooner’s put the mockers on his namesake resort

indicators.note: Rev Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

blocks.clueFragment: put the mockers on his namesake
blocks.note: to put the mockers on is to jinx or hex; Spooner was William, so his namesake is a Bill

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner curses another man of the same name at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: To put the mockers on is British slang for jinxing. Bexhill-on-Sea is a seaside resort in East Sussex, the B town in The ABC Murders.
explanation.definitionFit: Bexhill-on-Sea is an English seaside town where people go on holiday, so it is a resort.

clue.text: Hotel transfer’s despatched at least

indicators.note: what is despatched is sent away, so that letter leaves

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a handover is a transfer, with 's read as is

explanation.surface: A hotel's transfer has at least been sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: Andover, the Hampshire town, is the A in Christie's The ABC Murders; the enumeration splits it into a phrase. 'Transfer's' is 'transfer is' with H removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a number 'and over', as in eighteen and over, means that figure or more, the minimum.
